subject: Quick Q: data processing locations, subprocessors & deletion timelines for Keystone Health

Subject: Quick Q: data processing locations and subprocessors

Hi Rishi,

We’re evaluating Redwood for a couple of internal integrations and I have a couple of quick questions on the data flow: where (which cloud regions) does Redwood process API requests and derived artifacts (embeddings, logs, caches)? Which subprocessors are involved for hosted vs dedicated deployments?

Also: do you have an explicit cross-border flow map? We operate in multiple states and in the EU via a subsidiary, so we need to understand if any data transits outside of the US/EU and what controls you rely on (SCCs, contractual clauses, encryption-at-rest etc.).

Finally — retention & deletion: what are your default retention periods for request payloads, embeddings, and system logs, and how quickly do you honor deletion requests?

Can you send a short written summary or a diagram we can include in our security review? I’ve CC’d procurement so they have visibility.

Thanks,
Emily

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below; I can put together a short diagram and the subprocessor inventory for your security team. If useful we can book 30 minutes to walk through.

- Processing regions (hosted API): primary regions are US (us-west-2) and EU (eu-west-1). Requests are routed based on customer region preference and capacity policy; for some latency-sensitive customers we pin routing to a single region. Dedicated (reserved) capacity is customer-specific and runs in the region you select; Private (VPC/on-prem) runs in your environment only.

- Subprocessors (hosted): our primary cloud providers are AWS (compute + storage in the regions above), Google Cloud (for certain GPU capacity in burst scenarios), and Cloudflare (CDN and edge routing). We also use a managed logging provider for aggregated logs. For Dedicated we still use some cloud infra providers for control-plane telemetry unless you opt for Private where we can remove those.

- Cross-border transfers: for Hosted we rely on contractual safeguards (SCCs where applicable) and encryption in transit + at rest. Data can be replicated between US and EU for failover/DR in high-availability configurations; replication only occurs with customer opt-in or where routing policy requires it.

- Retention/deletion (hosted defaults): request payloads and temporary artifacts: 30 days default (configurable down to 0 for higher tiers); embeddings and model-derived artifacts: 90 days default; aggregated system logs/metrics: 365 days. We honor deletion/API purge requests for hosted customers within 72 hours once validated. For Dedicated, retention is governed by the reservation agreement — many customers choose shorter retention windows and we support a 30-day SLA for deletion on request. Private deployments are subject to the customer's own retention controls.

I’ll attach a short processing map and our subprocessor inventory; I’ll loop in our legal lead (Laura Bennett) for the SCC and deletion SLA language and follow up with that wording.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra

Hi Emily — following up with the consolidated answers and references from legal below. Apologies for the delay; Laura added the specifics.

1) Embeddings & deletion: our hosted deletion SLA covers model-derived artifacts, including embeddings, unless otherwise contracted. For hosted customers we remove embeddings and associated vectors within 72 hours of a validated deletion request. If you have PHI, we recommend a Dedicated or Private deployment so retention can be constrained to your policy and to avoid any optional cross-region replication.

2) KV/prefix cache: the runtime-level KV cache is considered ephemeral and is dropped on model instance termination. For hosted services, a deletion request will trigger cache invalidation immediately for active instances and a purge from persisted short-term caches within 72 hours. If you require immediate irrevocable deletion at the storage layer we can discuss a contractual addendum.

3) SCCs & transfer controls: we provide Standard Contractual Clauses (Controller-Processor + Processor-Subprocessor as applicable). The legal reference for SCCs and the executed agreement for templates is stored in our contract repo; Laura included the DocuSign reference below. Data in transit and at rest is always TLS-encrypted; at-rest encryption keys are managed by Redwood for hosted customers (with KMS integrations available for Dedicated/Private).

4) Processing map & subprocessors: attached are the processing map and the subprocessor inventory. Key subprocessors by function: compute/storage: AWS (us-west-2, eu-west-1), burst GPU: GCP (europe-west4), edge/CDN: Cloudflare, logging & observability: ManagedLogCo (US), identity & SSO: Okta. We can provide region-scoped inventories if you prefer.

Attachments: Redwood-Data-Processing-Map-2027.pdf; Redwood-Subprocessor-Invent-2027.csv; SOC2-Type2-2026-redacted.pdf

DocuSign reference (executed SCC template): https://docusign.example.com/exec/KHS-SCC-2027-14
